name: Halicarnassus
summary: Carian capital of Mausolus and site of the Mausoleum, one of the seven wonders.

name: Hamath
summary: Neo-Hittite and Aramaean royal city on the Orontes, later famed for its norias.

name: Harran
summary: Moon-god city of Sin that kept its pagan cult and astronomy into Islamic times.

name: Hasanlu
summary: Fortified Iron Age citadel violently destroyed, source of the famous gold bowl.

name: Hatra
summary: Fortified Parthian-era caravan and temple city that twice repulsed Rome before Sasanian destruction.

name: Hazor
summary: The largest Canaanite city in the southern Levant, with a huge lower town and archive.

name: Hegra
summary: Nabataean southern city of monumental rock tombs on the incense road.

name: Heshbon
summary: Moabite-Ammonite frontier town on the King's Highway.

name: Hierapolis
summary: Thermal spa and healing city abandoned after an earthquake.

name: Emesa

name: Imgur-Enlil

name: Isfahan
summary: Seljuk capital with a great congregational mosque, later Safavid Iran's showpiece.

name: Istakhr
summary: Sasanian-era Fars capital and early Islamic city near Persepolis, later eclipsed by Shiraz.

name: Jaffa

name: Gerasa
summary: Best-preserved Decapolis city, with oval forum and colonnaded cardo.

name: Jericho
summary: Earliest known walled settlement, with a stone tower a thousand years before farming villages spread.

name: Jerusalem
summary: Temple city sacred to three faiths and the political heart of Judah.

name: Julfar
summary: Pearl and Indian Ocean port of the lower Gulf, base of the navigator Ibn Majid.

name: Kanesh

name: Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta
summary: Short-lived Middle Assyrian royal city opposite Assur, abandoned on its founder's murder.

name: Karahan Tepe

name: Karatepe

name: Kashan

name: Kerman
summary: Sasanian foundation controlling the southeast trade route to India.

name: Khaybar

name: Kir-Hareseth
summary: Moabite stronghold, later a great Crusader and Mamluk castle town.

name: Kish
summary: First city to hold kingship after the flood in Sumerian tradition; Sargon's launching point.

name: Konar Sandal
summary: Monumental centre of the Halil Rud culture, a possible independent Bronze Age civilisation.

name: Iconium
summary: Ancient Phrygian town that became the Seljuk sultanate's capital and Rumi's home.

name: Kufa

name: Kussara
summary: Original royal seat of the Hittite dynasty; site not yet identified.

name: Kutha
summary: Cult city of the underworld god Nergal.

name: Lachish

name: Lagash

summary: Seleucid port that became coastal Syria's main outlet.

name: Larak
summary: Antediluvian city of the king list, location still disputed.

name: Masada
summary: Herodian desert palace-fortress and site of the Zealots' last stand; a fortress, not a city.

summary: Second city of Larsa, abandoned intact and so a rare full Old Babylonian town plan.

name: Mecca

name: Medina
summary: Oasis town that hosted Muhammad's community and became the first Islamic capital.

name: Megiddo

name: Melitene
summary: Euphrates frontier legionary city guarding the Anatolian passes.

name: Yumuktepe
summary: Long-lived Cilician mound with one of the earliest fortified settlements.

name: Miletus
summary: Ionian trading power, mother of dozens of colonies and birthplace of Greek philosophy.

name: Mleiha
summary: Inland southeast Arabian centre with monumental tombs and its own coinage.

name: Mosul

name: Mtskheta
summary: Ancient Iberian capital where Georgia adopted Christianity.

name: Najran

name: Nevalı Çori

name: Nicaea

name: Nicomedia
summary: Diocletian's eastern imperial capital before Constantinople.

name: Nisibis

name: Palmyra
summary: Desert caravan metropolis that under Zenobia briefly ruled the Roman East.

name: Pasargadae
summary: Cyrus the Great's first Persian capital, garden palace complex and his tomb.

name: Pergamon
summary: Attalid capital of the Great Altar and a library rivalling Alexandria's.

name: Perge
summary: Pamphylian city of colonnaded streets and monumental nymphaeum.

name: Persepolis
summary: Achaemenid ceremonial capital of the Apadana reliefs, burned by Alexander.

name: Pessinus
summary: Cult city of Cybele whose sacred stone was carried to Rome.

name: Petra
summary: Nabataean rock-cut capital that taxed the incense trade and mastered desert hydraulics.

name: Phocaea
summary: Ionian seafaring city that founded Massalia and much of the western Greek coast.

name: Priene
summary: Model Hellenistic grid city on terraces above the Maeander.

name: Qana
summary: Hadrami port of the Periplus shipping incense to Egypt and India.

name: Qaryat al-Faw
summary: Caravan city and Kindah capital at the mouth of the Wadi al-Dawasir pass.

name: Qatna
summary: Bronze Age kingdom whose intact royal tomb held gold, ivory and ancestor cult remains.

name: Qazvin
summary: Sasanian fortress town, later a frontier city against the Daylamites and Assassins.

name: Qom
summary: Shrine city of Fatima Masumeh and a centre of Shi'i learning.

name: Qumran
summary: Sectarian settlement linked to the Dead Sea Scrolls; a community compound, not a city.

name: Raqqa
summary: Harun al-Rashid's residence and a major Abbasid ceramic and garrison city.

name: Ray
summary: One of the plateau's greatest ancient cities, ruined by the Mongols and absorbed by Tehran.

name: Samaria

name: Samarra

name: Sana'a
summary: Highland capital of tower houses, seat of Yemeni states from Himyar onward.

name: Sardis
summary: Lydian capital of Croesus where coinage was invented, later a Roman provincial city.

name: Sarissa
summary: Planned Hittite provincial city with temple archives, founded and abandoned inside the empire's life.

name: Seleucia on the Tigris

name: Sepphoris
summary: Galilean city where the Mishnah was redacted, rich in mosaics.

name: Shabwa

name: Shahr-e Sukhteh
summary: Large eastern Iranian city with craft workshops, an artificial eye and early animation vessel.

name: Shamakhi
summary: Shirvanshah capital and silk-trade centre on the Caspian route.

name: Shechem
summary: Hill-country covenant city and first Israelite northern capital.

name: Shibam
summary: Mudbrick high-rise city, the earliest example of vertical urban planning.

name: Shiloh
summary: Pre-monarchic Israelite sanctuary that housed the Ark before Jerusalem.

name: Shiraz
summary: Islamic-era Fars capital of poets, gardens and wine.

name: Shuruppak
summary: Home of the flood hero Ziusudra and of the earliest wisdom instructions.

name: Side
summary: Pamphylian port that grew rich as a Cilician pirate market and grain harbour.

name: Sumur
summary: Egyptian administrative base on the Canaanite coast, prominent in the Amarna letters.

name: Sinope
summary: Best harbour on the Black Sea's south coast and Mithridates' birthplace.

name: Sippar
summary: Cult city of Shamash with a temple archive central to Babylonian law and scholarship.

name: Siraf
summary: Gulf port that dominated Abbasid trade with India and China until an earthquake ruined it.

name: Sirwah
summary: Early Sabaean centre with the Karib'il Watar inscription and oval temple.

name: Smyrna
summary: Aegean port with a claim on Homer, refounded by Alexander's successors as a great Roman city.

name: Sohar
summary: Oman's copper and Indian Ocean trading port, Sindbad's traditional home.

name: Sumhuram
summary: Hadrami frankincense port shipping Dhofar resin to Rome and India.

name: Tabriz
summary: Ilkhanid capital and the greatest Silk Road market of the Mongol west.

name: Ta'if
summary: Highland fruit-growing town and summer refuge for Mecca's elite.

name: Shiz
summary: Sasanian fire-temple sanctuary city around a volcanic lake; largely ceremonial.

name: Tarim
summary: Hadrami centre of Sufi scholarship that seeded Islam across the Indian Ocean.

name: Tarsus
summary: Cilician capital, a great school city and Paul's birthplace.

name: Tayma
summary: Walled north Arabian oasis where Nabonidus of Babylon lived in self-exile.

name: Tbilisi
summary: Kura crossing capital of Georgia and a Silk Road meeting point.

name: Teishebaini
summary: Last great Urartian administrative citadel, burned by Scythians or Medes.

name: Dan
summary: Israelite cult city with a mudbrick gate arch and the earliest extrabiblical mention of David.

name: Tell al-Ubaid
summary: Type-site of the Ubaid culture that seeded southern Mesopotamian urbanism.

name: Tell Brak
summary: One of the oldest cities anywhere, with the Eye Temple and a Hurrian-Akkadian palace.

name: Tell es-Sawwan
summary: Walled Samarran village showing the first irrigation farming on the Tigris; not a city.

name: Tell Halaf
summary: Type-site of Halaf painted pottery, later an Aramaean capital of carved orthostats.

name: Tell Leilan
summary: Shamshi-Adad's Upper Mesopotamian capital, abandoned after a drought collapse.

name: Urkesh

summary: Northern Mesopotamian mound documenting the rise of temples and seals before writing.

name: Tepe Hissar
summary: Northern Iranian craft and metal town on the route to Central Asia.

name: Tepe Sialk
summary: Long-lived plateau mound with a ziggurat-like platform and early metallurgy.

name: Tepe Yahya
summary: Chlorite-working town linking Mesopotamia, Elam and the Indus.

name: Terqa
summary: Middle Euphrates town of Dagan's temple, closely tied to Mari.

name: Thaj
summary: Walled Hellenistic-era eastern Arabian city, possibly the Gerrha of Greek sources.

name: Tiberias
summary: Rabbinic capital where the Jerusalem Talmud and Masoretic text were codified.

name: Tigranocerta
summary: Tigranes the Great's showpiece capital, sacked by Lucullus soon after founding.

name: Tikrit
summary: Fortress town on the Tigris, a Syriac Christian seat and Saladin's birthplace.

name: Timna
summary: Industrial copper-smelting camp complex, not a city.

name: Tirzah
summary: Early capital of the northern Israelite kingdom before Samaria.

name: Trapezus
summary: Black Sea silk-route terminus and capital of the last Byzantine successor empire.

name: Tripoli
summary: Phoenician federal port, later a Crusader county and Mamluk centre of paper and sugar.

name: Tus
summary: Khorasani city of Firdawsi and al-Ghazali, ruined by Timurid warfare.

name: Tushpa
summary: Rock-citadel capital of Urartu with royal cuneiform annals and vast canal works.

name: Tuttul
summary: Bronze Age city at the Balikh confluence, a cult seat of Dagan.

name: Ubar
summary: Caravan waterhole and fort of the incense route, identified with legendary Iram.

name: Ugarit
summary: Canaanite port whose alphabetic cuneiform archives preserved West Semitic myth; destroyed in the Bronze Age collapse.

name: Umma
summary: Sumerian rival of Lagash in the earliest recorded border war.

name: Ur
summary: Third-Dynasty imperial capital with a great ziggurat and lavish royal tombs.

name: Veh-Ardashir
summary: Sasanian round city facing Ctesiphon, a major Christian and Jewish centre.

name: Wasit
summary: Umayyad administrative city midway on the Tigris, abandoned as the river shifted.

name: Xanthos
summary: Chief city of Lycia, famed for pillar tombs and its own written language.

name: Yazd
summary: Desert silk city of wind-catchers and a stronghold of Zoroastrianism.

name: Yazılıkaya
summary: Rock sanctuary of the Hittite pantheon beside Hattusa; ceremonial, not a city.

name: Zabalam
summary: Early cult centre of Inanna listed among the oldest Sumerian towns.

name: Zabid

name: Zafar
summary: Highland capital of Himyar, which unified Yemen and adopted monotheism.

name: Sam'al
summary: Aramaean-Luwian royal city with a circular wall and Aramaic funerary stelae.

name: Arwad

summary: The northernmost city, on an island off the Syrian coast.

name: Byblos

name: Sidon
